column1: # The corpus: which replays it is made of, and what each one does.
# the beatmap ids by `tools/fetch-maps.py --manifest <this file>`. Do not
# edit by hand — a row that disagrees with what the engine measures is
# worse than no row at all.
# ── what this file is, and what it is not ────────────────────────────────
# A change detector, not a claim that any of it is right. Sixty-three of the
# rows below record a disagreement with the client that played the replay, and
# writing them down is how a change to any of them gets noticed — including a
# change for the better. A row of zeros is agreement; a row with numbers in it
# is a number the engine is expected to be wrong by *today*.
# It was rewritten on 2026-09-01 because it had stopped working. The corpus was
# lost and restored once, and the restored replays hash differently: of 134
# rows, 33 still matched a replay on disk, 101 named replays that were gone and
# 112 replays were watched by nothing. A manifest that covers a quarter of the
# The largest disagreements as it stands, count error first:
#      46      0    -3.81  goprob … Guilty All The Same                   Relax

# eight replays. The presses are synthesised because the game does not record
